head: working-tree
intent: Move Rust sources to crates, move TypeScript workspaces to packages, remove the source apps directory, add reproducible Nix packaging and a NixOS module, and refresh repository documentation.

findings.summary: The initial shared service policy made all of /zos and /run/zos writable by every service and left root hostd without the Debian unit's capability bound.
The default terminal service lacked the required passwd home and interactive shell, while optional Bluetooth and VOD services lacked runtime setup used by the native Debian units.
Disabled ZOS integrations initially forced Docker, libvirt, and Bluetooth to false, conflicting with independent system-level NixOS definitions.
The module exposed an external Nginx listener but provided no explicit firewall contract, so the documented LAN endpoint could remain unreachable on a default NixOS firewall.
Share and Docker daemon write controls became enabled when their first capability request failed instead of failing closed until write capability was known.

appliedFixes: matched Nix service write paths, capability bounds, resource limits, dependencies, and runtime identities to the established native service boundaries
configured the terminal account home and shell plus Bluetooth, VOD, and host-access runtime prerequisites
made optional host integrations additive so disabled ZOS options do not override external NixOS ownership
added an explicit nginx.openFirewall option with a secure default and documented deployment behavior
made UI mutation controls require an affirmative server capability
added NixOS VM assertions for service write paths, root hostd capability bounds, and the terminal account

advisories.summary: The full Nix package closure and NixOS VM derivation were evaluated but not built locally; native x86_64-linux and aarch64-linux CI remain authoritative.

verification.nixWorkspaceLayoutBuild: passed before the final module-only review fixes
